text: The main statements of the draft with their status. Numbers refer to the version of the paper on this site; a number opens the paper at the statement, and the links in the text lead to the computation, the code and data (commit e385617), the Lean files and the open questions. computer: checked by an exact computation (lattices modulo $p^E$ in Howell form, or the truncated Magnus algebra, with the exactness certificate); paper: proved; Lean: formally verified.
Status · Statement · Where

Lean · Reduction: $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for all groups $\iff$ $D_5(Q)=1$ for all finite $2$-groups of class $3$. For finite $G$ the order does not grow: $2$-groups up to the $2$-part of $|G|$ suffice. Proved in Lean without hypotheses: Passi's theorem ($D_4^2\subseteq\gamma_4$), Gruenberg's theorem and $D_3=\gamma_3$ are proved there too. · Prop. 2.1, Rem. 2.3; Lean
Lean · For Lie rings $D_5(L)\subseteq\gamma_4(L)$ (Ionin, Mikhailov, Petrov, 2026); the formalization audited, the group question stated in Lean next to it. · §3, §4

computer + paper · $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every finite $G$ with Sylow $2$-subgroup of order $\le2^{10}$, in particular for all groups of order $<2048$. That all $3400$ candidates of order $2^{10}$ have $D_4=D_5=1$ is also checked in Lean, by certificates (via native_decide); the completeness of the list is Lemma 5.2(d) and the ANUPQ computation. · Thm. 5.4(1); Prop. 5.3; Lean

computer + paper · Order $2^{11}$, class $3$: $D_5=1$ for every rank — ranks $2$–$7$ by search, $\ge8$ without search (every candidate has $|\Phi(Q)|\ge16$ on paper, and in Lean as: no candidate has $|P_2(Q)|\le8$; the passage to candidates is via Prop. 5.3; given $D_3=\gamma_3$ and that proposition, the $D_5$ statement is also proved in Lean, with the inclusion of Jennings' theorem that is needed ($p=2$, $n=5$, class $\le3$)). A counterexample, if any, has order $\ge2^{12}$. The $2^{10}$ search and ranks $2$–$4$, $7$, $8$ were repeated with ANUPQ with the audit fixes: the results agree exactly. · Prop. 5.10, Prop. 5.7; Lean; Lean ($D_5$)

Lean · Central products: $D_n(H\circ E)=D_n(H)$ for $E\in\{D_8,Q_8\}$ and $t\in\gamma_2(H)$, and for $E=M_{2^{k+2}}$ under a condition on $g^{-2}s$ (e.g. $s=g^2$). All $386$ candidates of orders $2^6$–$2^9$ satisfy it, so splitting off $E\in\{D_8,Q_8,M_{16}\}$ gives no counterexample. Gluing along a proper subgroup of $Z(E)$ is closed when $\sigma=g^{2^{j+1}}$ (a central root of any degree; the rest is open); each of the $20$ split candidates has a splitting covered by Prop. 5.8. Prop. 5.8 and Lemma 5.9 are proved in Lean; the check of the candidates is by computer. · Prop. 5.8, Lemma 5.9
computer · $D_n(G)=\gamma_n(G)$ for all $n$ and every finite group of order $<512$. · Thm. 5.4(2)
computer + paper · No $3$-torsion in $D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)$ when the Sylow $3$-subgroup of $G$ has order $\le3^9$; $D_5=\gamma_5$ for all $3$-groups of order $\le3^9$. · Thm. 6.19
Lean · $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is finite of exponent $3$, of any rank and order. Proved in Lean, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1 on which the proof relies. · Thm. 6.6; Lean

Lean · More generally: $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)\cong C_{3^a}\times C_3^{s-1}$, i.e. it has at most one invariant larger than $3$ (including $C_9\times C_3^{s-1}$). Checked by an independent review and proved in Lean, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1. · Thm. 6.8; Lean

Lean · More generally still: $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group and $\gamma_2(G)/\gamma_3(G)$ has exponent $3$, whatever the invariants of $G/\gamma_2(G)$ (e.g. $C_9\times C_9\times C_3$ when $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ has exponent $3$); Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 are corollaries. Checked by an independent review and proved in Lean, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1. Hence a minimal counterexample has $\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)\ge9$ and $\gamma_4\le Z$ cyclic. · Thm. 6.9; Lean

Lean · Further still: $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group, $\gamma_4(G)^3\subseteq\gamma_5(G)$ and $\gamma_2(G)^9\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$; Theorem 6.9 is the special case, and $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_3/\gamma_4$ may now have exponent $9$. Checked by an independent review and proved in Lean, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1. Hence a minimal counterexample with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ has $x,y$ with $[x^9,y]\notin\gamma_4$, i.e. $\gamma_2^9\not\subseteq\gamma_4$. · Thm. 6.10; Lean

Lean · Most general so far: $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group and $\gamma_4(G)^3\subseteq\gamma_5(G)$, with no condition on the exponents of $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_3/\gamma_4$; Theorems 6.9 and 6.10 are special cases. The proof and the Lean code were checked by independent reviews; proved in Lean, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1. Hence $D_5(Q)\subseteq\gamma_4(Q)^3$ for every finite $3$-group of class $\le4$ (Corollary 6.12), and a minimal counterexample has $\gamma_4\cong C_{3^k}$ with $k\ge2$ and $D_5=\Omega_1(\gamma_4)$. · Thm. 6.11; Lean

Lean · Beyond the paper: $D_5(Q)=1$ for every finite group $Q$ of class $\le4$ with $Q/\gamma_2(Q)\cong C_3\times C_9\times C_9$, with no condition on $\gamma_4$; in particular for $\gamma_4\cong C_9$, where Theorem 6.11 does not apply (Remark 6.13). Proved through the exact identity $(\star)$ and Tahara's Theorem 6.1; checked by a review and proved in Lean. For other types of $Q_{ab}$ with $\gamma_4\cong C_9$ the question is open. · Blueprint; Lean

Lean · $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $p$-group, $p$ odd, and $[\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\subseteq\gamma_5$ (e.g. $G$ metabelian), with no condition on $\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)$; at $p=3$, for metabelian $G$, this is Gupta–Tahara [GT85, Thm. 3.2(c)]. Proved through Tahara's Theorem 6.1, checked by an independent review and proved in Lean; hence Lemmas 6.1 (at $p=3$) and 6.2 without hypotheses. · Thm. D.1; Lean

Lean · $p$ odd, $|\gamma_3/\gamma_4|=p$, $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ with at most two generators $\Rightarrow$ $[\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\subseteq\gamma_5$. Hence a non-metabelian $p$-group of class $4$ and rank $d$ has order $\ge p^{d+5}$. · Lemma 6.3, Prop. 6.5; Lean

Lean · $p$ odd, $P$ of class $3$ with $|\gamma_2/\gamma_3|=p^2$, $|\gamma_3|=p$ $\Rightarrow$ the $p$-covering group has $P^{*\prime\prime}=1$: all step-$1$ descendants are metabelian. In Lean for every central extension of $P$ by a subgroup of exponent $p$ (Mathlib has no $p$-covering group). · Thm. 6.15; Lean

computer + paper · $p$ odd, $P$ of type $(d,2,1)$ with $P/\gamma_2$ elementary: $P$ is nonterminal (has immediate descendants) exactly when N1–N3 hold and the system (E)+(J) is solvable with $c\ne0$. Checked by computer: at $3^8$ the criterion picks out exactly the $190$ nonterminal groups among $7\,824$; at $3^7$, $5^7$, $7^7$ exactly $102$, $110$, $118$. · Thm. 6.17
computer · Class-$3$ quotients of Rips-type groups of orders $2^{40}$–$2^{107}$: $D_5=1$ in all, $D_4\ne1$ in three of them (with the exactness certificate). · §7, question 1

computer · Rips's group (order $2^{38}$, from Tahara's 1978 presentation): $D_4=\{1,y_1^{128}\}$, and every proper subgroup has $D_4=1$; $26\,147$ random quotients (with repetitions) also have $D_4=1$, and a heuristic hill climb over the exponents of Tahara's presentation found nothing below $2^{38}$. The sections checked give no calibration below $2^{38}$ (proper sections $H/N$ with $H\lt G$, $N\ne1$ not checked; code). · §5

computer · $3$-torsion: the Bartholdi–Mikhailov $3$-group with $D_7
e\gamma_7$ has order $3^{494}$, but its three quotients by central subgroups of order $3$ not containing the witness $\omega$ have order $3^{493}$ and $D_7
e\gamma_7$, so $3^{494}$ is not the least order of a $3$-group with $D_7
e\gamma_7$; every proper quotient of these three groups kills $\omega$. That $\omega\in D_7$ follows from Bartholdi–Mikhailov's Prop. 9.2 via the map (not onto) from their group (9.2) to $G$. Subgroups of either group are checked only against BM's argument and only for $H\ge\Phi(Q)\langle x_1,\dots,x_4angle$; other subgroups, other arguments, and new witnesses in quotients, not checked (code). · §5

computer · $3$-torsion: a $3$-group with $D_n\ne\gamma_n$ (for some $n$) has order $\ge3^{10}$. A least-order example has cyclic centre and its socle lies in $D_{c+1}\cap Q''\cap M_{c+1}$ ($c$ the class); class $4$ is settled up to $3^9$ by the $D_5$ theorem, and all $1035$ groups of order $3^6$–$3^8$ and class $\ge5$ that meet these conditions, and all $27\,547$ such groups of order $3^9$ (step-$1$ descendants of groups of order $3^8$), have $D_{c+1}=1$ (code). · §7, question 2
computer · The group analogue of Theorem C at $c=4$: the plateau group has $D_6\ne1$ but $D_7=1$, so $2c-2$ is attained and the analogue, if true, is sharp (an open question). · §7, question 3

computer · A lower bound for $D_4\ne\gamma_4$: such a $2$-group has order $\ge2^{11}$, so $D_4(G)=\gamma_4(G)$ for every finite $G$ with Sylow $2$-subgroup of order $\le2^{10}$. The smallest known example is Rips's group, of order $2^{38}$. Order $2^{10}$: the condition $n\in D_4$ on the $p$-covering group is linear in the hyperplane $U$ (Nakayama's lemma), and none of the $10\,208\,630$ parents of order $2^9$ has a $U$ with $n\in D_4$ (code). · §5
